findings.message: Criterion 2 and the Scope-in require the committed GO-grade report to 'accept only GO or NO-GO', and the receipt verdict must come from it. The merged `ReviewBaselineReport` schema (squatch/artifacts.py:214-224) and the committed report have no verdict field: only defect count, spend, tickets, graph, scored_summary and `verdict_signal_identity`. The harness hard-codes `VERDICT = "NO-GO"` (eval/harness.py:64). A GO exists only as an operator-recorded `review_baseline` journal signal via `--record-go`, which is not a committed artifact. Section 20 says the exit 'reads the committed GO-grade report and its embedded verdict identity, accepts GO or NO-GO' but never defines how the verdict is derived. As written, `go_grade_verdict` can only be invented, which the ticket's own Definition of rejected forbids.
findings.paved_road: fix the plan, then re-author the ticket

findings.message: The merged `ExitReceipt.go_grade_verdict` is `Literal["GO", "NO_GO"]`, but the criteria and Scope-in say 'GO or NO-GO', which matches the harness spelling `NO-GO`. A test written to the ticket's wording would fail against the merged receipt schema. The ticket also never defines the algorithm for `host_loop_digest`.
findings.paved_road: fix the plan, then re-author the ticket

findings.message: The ticket says the `HOST_LOOP_REPORT` / `EXIT_RECEIPT` closed ordinary-lane writers are in `squatch/artifacts.py`. In fact artifacts.py holds only the names and schemas; they are registered as writers in `squatch/stages.py`'s `KNOWN_ARTIFACTS` (lines 95-96).
